# Write roster-coverage and pairing-invariant tests for 10-level campaign

## Goal

Add automated tests that enforce the campaign's core invariants before the new levels exist (tests will fail until Levels 6–10 are added), ensuring the plan is test-first.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Roster coverage test** — A test iterates the merged 10-level campaign (via ) and asserts every one of the eight classic-arcade archetypes (, , , , , , , ) appears in at least one wave group. The test initially fails (campaign has only 5 levels) and passes after Levels 6–10 are added.
2. **Player-targeter pairing invariant** — A test iterates every wave of every level and asserts that any wave containing a player-targeting archetype (, , , ) also contains at least one non-player-targeting enemy kind. The test is parameterised by the targeter set so it can evolve.

data.description:
# Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game — Intake Brief

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** task · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The Power Pellet is a Pac-Man-inspired power-up that opens a timed "fright
window": every live enemy flees the ship, stops firing, and can be rammed for a
free kill. It is no longer wanted in the game. The player should not be able to
obtain or use it, and (per the producer decision on this item) the whole
mechanic should be removed — catalogue entry, drop weight, hold-full choice,
level specs, HUD/icon surfaces, bot valuation, and the shared frightened-enemy
status layer — rather than hidden or retained. The **Pac-Man ghost enemy family
is a separate archetype and must keep working unchanged**; it does not depend on
the fright machinery.

## Users

- **Player** (primary): expects the drop pool and hold-full choices to offer
  only the intended power-ups; the Power Pellet must no longer appear or alter
  enemy behaviour.
- **Designer / maintainer** (secondary): needs the removal to be complete and
  traceable — no dead code, no orphaned tests, and a clear note in the
  classic-arcade research record explaining why a previously shipped concept is
  gone.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I never receive a Power Pellet from a destroyed enemy or from a
  hold-full choice, so the enemy set behaves predictably.
- As a maintainer, I can search the codebase for `power_pellet` and find no
  shipped references, so I do not have to reason about a half-removed feature.
- As a maintainer, the Pac-Man ghosts still chase, ambush, flank and wander
  exactly as before, so removing the pellet does not regress the enemy roster.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Power Pellet is removed from every player-facing catalogue/selection
  surface: `power_pellet` no longer appears in `PowerUpId`, `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`
  or `COMBAT_POWER_UP_IDS`; in `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS`/`defaultPowerUpWeights()`;
  in `CHOICE_POOL`; in the power-up level specs, level-variable union and
  `PowerUpLevelStats`; in the HUD power-up mapping; in the power-up icons; or in
  the competent-bot drop valuations.
- The shared frightened-enemy status layer is removed: `src/scenes/core/frightenedState.ts`
  is deleted and its playbook is not re-created elsewhere; `EffectsRegistry`
  no longer exposes `isFrightened`, `frightenElapsed` or
  `frightenSpeedMultiplier`; and the flee-offset, fire-suppression and
  ram-destroys-frightened-enemy branches are removed from `CombatCoreScene`,
  `CombatScene`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`, `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymLevel` and `GymBoss` (including
  the `suppressed` parameter on `fireForEnemy`).
- No dangling references remain in shipped source or configuration: a repo-wide
  search for `power_pellet`, `powerPellet`, `frighten`/`frightened` and `Power
  Pellet` finds no shipped (non-test) reference; TypeScript typecheck, lint and
  build pass.
- Testing/validation: Power Pellet-specific tests are deleted and the affected
  suites are updated to assert the removal — in particular a regression test
  proves `power_pellet` is absent from the catalogue, default weights and
  `CHOICE_POOL`, so the power-up cannot be spawned or offered.
- Ghost parity is preserved: the Pac-Man ghost family (`src/entities/Ghost.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/ghostSteering.ts`, `src/waves/GhostSpawner.ts`, configs
  `ghost-chase`/`ghost-ambush`/`ghost-flank`/`ghost-wander`) continues to run
  its personality steering and scatter/chase cycle, and no ghost test regresses.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries:
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` records the Pac-Man Power Pellet as
  removed/reverted with the reason; the Game Design Document §4.4/§8 and the
  README roster drop it from the shipped list; and the header comments in
  `src/powerups/types.ts` / `src/utils/weapons.ts` no longer list it.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the removal must be applied to the shared core and every
  gym in the same change; no scene may keep a divergent copy of the fright
  behaviour. See `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1.
- **Do not touch the ghosts:** `Ghost.ts`, `ghostSteering.ts` and
  `GhostSpawner.ts` must continue to compile and behave identically; the fright
  layer is applied generically at scene level, so removing it must not alter
  non-frightened enemy movement.
- **No scope creep:** this item removes the Power Pellet only. It must not
  rebalance the remaining power-ups' weights beyond deleting the pellet entry,
  nor change the other classic-arcade power-ups/weapons. Any further removal or
  tuning discovered during implementation becomes a linked work item.
- **Traceability:** the removal is recorded in the research doc per producer
  decision Q2=A. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (release pipeline).
- **No git-history rewriting:** the feature and its tests are deleted in the
  normal way; history remains the recovery path.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpId` includes `power_pellet`; the catalogue
  has a `power_pellet` entry (`duration: 6`); `COMBAT_POWER_UP_IDS` cycles it.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `DEFAULT_POWER_PELLET_WEIGHT` (3) and the weight table
  include `power_pellet`.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL` includes `power_pellet`.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `frightenDuration` / `frightenSpeedMultiplier`
  variables + specs; the `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS` list and `PowerUpLevelStats` fields.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `applyCollect` `power_pellet` case; `isFrightened`,
  `frightenElapsed`, `frightenSpeedMultiplier`; imports `FRIGHTEN_DEFAULT_DURATION`.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — `ICON_COLORS.power_pellet`, a `drawPowerPellet`
  function and the switch case.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — the `power_pellet` case in the power-up readout.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — the bot's `{ id: 'power_pellet', value: 1.3 }` drop preference.
- `src/scenes/core/frightenedState.ts` — the whole pure fright policy module.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_frightenedFleeHeadings`,
  `isEnemyFrightened`, `_frightenedFleeOffset`, and the reset clearing of the map.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — the ram-destroys-frightened enemy branch.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — `fireForEnemy(..., suppressed)` and the
  fire-suppression doc/logic.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — flee-offset calls and fire suppression.
- Tests referencing the feature: `src/core/rules.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/icons.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/frightenedState.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts`.
- Docs-guard tests that assert the roster/research doc lists the Power Pellet:
  `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`, `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (§5, catalogue table, gym
  table, work-item table), `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 tables and the
  fright-window callouts, §8), `README.md` (roster + module descriptions),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (parity references).

## Desired change

Delete the Power Pellet and everything that exists only to serve it, in one
consistent change:

1. Remove the catalogue/id/weight/choice/level/HUD/icon/bot-valuation entries.
2. Delete `src/scenes/core/frightenedState.ts` and remove every consumer: the
   `EffectsRegistry` fright accessors, `CombatCoreScene`'s fright state, the
   `CombatScene` ram branch, `enemyFire`'s `suppressed` parameter, and each
   scene's flee-offset/suppression call.
3. Delete the Power Pellet tests and update the docs/roster guards to reflect the
   removal; add/retain a regression assertion that `power_pellet` is absent from
   catalogue, weights and choice pool.
4. Record the removal (reason + date) in the classic-arcade research doc and drop
   the pellet from the GDD/README shipped roster, keeping the ghosts and the
   other seven classic concepts intact.

**Key Files:**

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Remove `power_pellet` from `PowerUpId`,
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` and `COMBAT_POWER_UP_IDS`; drop it from the module doc.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Remove `DEFAULT_POWER_PELLET_WEIGHT`, the weight-table
  branch and the `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` entry.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — Remove `power_pellet` from `CHOICE_POOL`.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Remove the `frightenDuration`/
  `frightenSpeedMultiplier` variables, specs, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS` entry and
  `PowerUpLevelStats` fields.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Remove the `power_pellet` `applyCollect` case and
  the `isFrightened`/`frightenElapsed`/`frightenSpeedMultiplier` accessors plus
  the `frightenedState` import.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Remove the colour entry, switch case and
  `drawPowerPellet`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Remove the `power_pellet` readout case.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — Remove the bot's pellet drop value.
- `src/scenes/core/frightenedState.ts` — Delete the file (pure fright policy).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Remove fright imports, the flee-heading
  map, `isEnemyFrightened`, `_frightenedFleeOffset` and the reset clearing.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Remove the ram-destroys-frightened branch.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — Remove the `suppressed` parameter and its docs.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Remove the flee-offset call and both fire-suppression sites.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Remove the flee offset + suppression.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Remove the scout flee/suppression handling.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — Remove fire suppression.
- `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`, `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`
  — Update the roster/research guards to the post-removal state.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Record the removal and
  drop the pellet from the shipped roster.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1BIW95004POSX** — Pac-Man power pellet fright (the feature being
  removed; completed, shipped in the classic-arcade arsenal).
- **AH-0MV4BXUWT005MWAJ** — Enemy arcs around player during power pellet (the
  flee-heading capture refinement, also removed with the feature).
- **AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4** — New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games
  (parent epic; seven other concepts remain shipped).
- **AH-0MV1BIXSH000JLN0** — Documentation integration for the classic arcade
  arsenal (owns the roster docs-guard tests that must be updated).
- **AH-0MV01EH2U008XT3Q** — Pac-Man personality-pursuer ghost enemies (the
  ghost archetype that must keep working; independent of the fright layer).
- Research catalogue: `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` §5 (Pac-Man
  power pellet).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the frightened status exists only to serve the Power Pellet,
  so it can be deleted wholesale. Verified by grep — `frightenedState.ts`,
  `isFrightened` and the suppression/flee paths have no other producer or
  consumer.
- **Assumption:** the ghosts do not depend on the fright layer. Verified —
  `Ghost.ts`, `ghostSteering.ts` and `GhostSpawner.ts` contain zero `frighten`
  references; the fright offset is applied generically at scene level.
- **Risk (roster/docs guards):** the Power Pellet is asserted present by
  `powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts` and `classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`;
  these must be updated in the same change or the suite fails.
- **Risk (weight redistribution):** deleting the pellet from the weight table
  changes the normalised drop shares of the remaining power-ups. Mitigate by
  keeping every other weight value unchanged (intent is removal, not rebalance)
  and updating only the tests that asserted the pellet's share.
- **Risk (incomplete removal):** a missed consumer (e.g. a gym or the bot
  valuation) would leave a compile error or a dead branch. Mitigate with a
  repo-wide grep as an explicit AC and a regression test asserting absence.
- **Risk (scope creep):** removing other classic power-ups/weapons, or adding a
  general "enemy status" seam, is out of scope; record any such opportunity as a
  linked work item. The recovered fright code remains in git history if a future
  power-up needs it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How far should the removal go — (A) full removal everywhere, (B)
  player-only with documented gym divergence, (C) disabled-by-default retaining
  code?** — Answer (operator, interactive): **A — full removal**, with the
  frightened-status code deleted. The operator first asked how the options
  affect the Pac-Man fright window and whether the ghosts keep working; the
  agent explained that the fright layer is a generic enemy debuff independent of
  the ghost archetype, and the operator then chose A. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: What should happen to the design/doc record that lists the Power Pellet
  as shipped — (A) record the removal, (B) delete all mentions?** — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **A — record the removal** in the research doc/GDD/
  README and update the roster docs-guard tests. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Should the shared frightened-enemy status code be deleted or retained as
  a generic enemy-status seam?** — Answer (operator, interactive): **"See 1"** —
  follows Q1's choice of full removal, so the code is deleted (recoverable from
  git history). Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP** – P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R3BM007ARY1** – Extract drop collection into CombatScene with collect hooks (completed)
- **AH-0MV1BIUGE005BJO8** – Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv14so0g0095ij4, 0mv1biw95004posx, able, absent, accessors (+355 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv14so0g0095ij4, 0mv1biw95004posx, able, absent, acceptance (+348 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv01eh2u008xt3q, 0mv14so0g0095ij4, able, absent, accessors (+312 more)

## Planning decision: auto-complete (no decomposition)

Step-1 heuristic applied: not an epic (`issueType: task`), measurable/testable ACs present, and a minimal implementation sketch present (the `Desired change` 4-point list plus the `**Key Files:**` map), and the item has no children. The whole removal is one atomic change (feature + consumers + tests + docs must land together to keep the build green), so splitting it into child items would create horizontal, non-buildable slices. No child work items created.

## Six review stages (existing content)

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — Each requirement traces to an AC: catalogue/weights/choice/levels/HUD/icons/bot-valuation AC; frightened-layer removal AC (file + EffectsRegistry accessors + consumers); no-dangling-references AC; testing/validation AC; ghost-parity AC; docs AC; full-suite AC. The three intake Appendix answers (Q1 full removal, Q2 record the removal, Q3 delete the fright code) are all reflected. No missing/contradictory/invented ACs found.
2. **Completeness** — Description, ACs, existing state, risks and related work are complete. `**Key Files:**` section is syntactically valid (every listed shipped path has a directory separator + extension; the root-level `README.md` is the only path without a separator and is intentional). Verified the "Existing state" against a repo-wide grep: all listed producers/consumers exist. Note (non-blocking): the test inventory omits `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts` (a `Power Pellet` fixture) and `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts` (has `frighten` assertions); both must be updated during implementation. `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` carries the `Pac-Man power pellet` guard as described.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — Single-item plan, so no inter-item sequence to order. Within the item the change is naturally ordered: catalogue/selection removal and frightened-layer deletion first, then test updates and docs, then the absence regression assertion. No dependency edges needed (no children).
4. **Scope sizing** — The item is one deliverable increment with a single commit boundary; no further split is deliverable without breaking enforcement (typecheck/lint/build). Within the no-scope-creep constraint (remove the pellet only, no re-weighting, 7 other classic concepts and the ghosts untouched).
5. **Acceptance & testability** — Every AC is pass/fail and mechanically checkable: repo-wide grep for the identifiers returns no shipped hits; typecheck/lint/build; targeted suites; the absence regression test; the ghost tests. The stale-stage guard is the grep AC plus the regression assertion.
6. **Polish & handoff** — Description is clear, well formatted and copy-pasteable; risks, assumptions and the Appendix are recorded. No open questions for the producer.

AC coverage review (`tree_coverage.apply_coverage_review`): `proceed` — parent ACs are the deliverable of this item itself, so no covering children are required; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

Plan: changelog — 2026-10-12: Step-1 auto-complete applied; six review stages recorded; no children created; stage set to `plan_complete`.
